description: Autocorrect behaviour version 2: what the computer ends with when the keyboard corrects a list while keys are typed. Rules: docs/spec/autocorrect-v1.md; each case names the rule it holds. A case has a list (entries as in autocorrect_domain_v2.json, each with how it fires), macros when a correction plays one (the text each stored macro types, by slot; a slot left out is empty), a host layout (a slug of host_layouts_v1.json), the host's Caps Lock at its start, and events. Events: {type: text} presses the keys that show those characters on that layout under that Caps Lock, one after another ('\n' is Enter, '\t' Tab); {fast: text} the same with no pause, so later keys arrive while a correction is typed; {key, mods} taps a named key; {stroke} taps a layout stroke; {tap} taps a key by its QMK name with whatever modifiers are held; {press} and {release} hold a modifier; {click}; {hold, ms, repeats} holds a key that long while the computer repeats it; {macro: text, fast} presses a macro key that types the text; {mash, count} taps a key that many times with no pause; {leader: true} presses the Leader key (D-F71); {wait: ms} lets that much time pass with no key; {override: bool} sets the autocorrect override, as AC_ON and AC_OFF do. result is the text the computer ends with; resultEndsWith holds only its end where the rest depends on timing. screen, when present, is the same input as the characters the computer would show with autocorrect off ('\b' is Backspace, U+0010 the Leader key): a client's text matcher run over it with the case's list, layout and Caps Lock must produce result. A case with keyboardOnly has no screen form and says why. The case folding and capitals are wordCharacters in autocorrect_domain_v2.json: a small letter's capital is the one character that folds to it. Test evidence, never a migration source.

cases.name: word-end-space
cases.description: A listed typo is corrected when Space ends the word.

cases.name: differing-suffix
cases.description: becuase becomes because: four characters erased, four typed.

cases.name: word-end-enter
cases.description: Enter ends the word; the correction comes first, then Enter.

cases.name: word-end-punctuation
cases.description: Punctuation and a hyphen end a word.

cases.name: inside-a-longer-word
cases.description: A whole-word typo inside a longer word is never touched.

cases.name: unfinished-word
cases.description: A typo in a word still being typed is left alone.

cases.name: apostrophe-after
cases.description: An apostrophe after the word stays on screen and is not part of the typo.

cases.name: apostrophes-around
cases.description: Apostrophes before and after the word stay.

cases.name: apostrophe-inside
cases.description: An apostrophe between letters is part of the word.

cases.name: digits-are-word-characters
cases.description: Digits belong to the word, so teh2 is not teh.

cases.name: shift-space
cases.description: Shift+Space types a space, so it ends the word.

cases.name: shift-enter
cases.description: Shift+Enter is typing too.

cases.name: two-typos-one-correction
cases.description: Two typos of one correction both become it.

cases.name: anywhere-in-a-word
cases.description: A typo that matches anywhere replaces only the matched part.

cases.name: end-of-a-word
cases.description: A typo that matches the end of a word, and not its start.

cases.name: start-of-a-word
cases.description: A typo that matches the start of a word, and not its end.

cases.name: longest-typo-wins
cases.description: Of two part-of-word typos that match, the longer wins.

cases.name: whole-word-beats-part
cases.description: A whole-word typo beats a part-of-word one that also matches.

cases.name: first-in-the-list-wins-a-tie
cases.description: Of two part-of-word typos of the same length, the one first in the list (the lower typo in byte order) wins.

cases.name: more-part-of-word-typos-than-one-step
cases.description: A list with more part-of-word typos than the keyboard compares in one scan (32): the ones past the first 32 still match, and the longest still wins.

cases.name: first-letter-capital
cases.description: First letter capital, the rest small: the correction's first letter is capitalized.

cases.name: all-capitals
cases.description: Two or more letters, all capitals: the correction in capitals.

cases.name: mixed-case
cases.description: Any other mix: the correction as written.

cases.name: correction-keeps-its-capitals
cases.description: A correction written with capitals keeps them, whether or not the typo began with one.

cases.name: capitals-of-a-capitalized-correction
cases.description: All capitals still wins over the correction's own capitals; nothing changes when the word already reads that way.

cases.name: case-of-the-matched-part
cases.description: Case is judged on the part of the word the typo matched.

cases.name: caps-lock
cases.description: With Caps Lock on the word reads in capitals, and the correction is typed so it does too.

cases.name: caps-lock-with-iphone
cases.description: Caps Lock on and Shift on the first letter: the word reads iPHONE, so the correction is typed as written, small letters through Shift.

cases.name: caps-lock-on-macos
cases.description: macOS shows capitals under Caps Lock whatever Shift does; a correction in capitals is typed.

cases.name: capital-the-layout-cannot-type
cases.description: The layout cannot type the capital form (ẞ on German Windows), so the correction is typed as written.

cases.name: dutch-dead-key-typed
cases.description: Dutch on macOS: the correction's é is typed as the layout does, a dead key then e.

cases.name: dutch-dead-key-read
cases.description: Dutch on macOS: a character composed with a dead key is read as that character.

cases.name: us-international-dead-apostrophe
cases.description: US International: the apostrophe is a dead key completed by Space. That Space is the apostrophe, not a word end.

cases.name: us-international-unresolved-dead-key
cases.description: A dead key the layout composes nothing with (apostrophe, then t) leaves the word unknown: nothing is corrected until the next word end.
cases.keyboardOnly: a dead-key sequence the layout does not resolve

cases.name: word-ended-through-a-dead-key
cases.description: A word ended by a character composed through a dead key (the quote on US-International is a dead key, then Space) is passed over: the dead key reached the computer before the word was known to have ended. The next word is replaced as usual.
cases.keyboardOnly: a word ended through a dead key

cases.name: dead-key-right-after-a-replacement
cases.description: A dead key pressed right after a replacement is still read: one the layout composes nothing with suspends the word it begins.
cases.keyboardOnly: a dead-key sequence the layout does not resolve

cases.name: undo-after-space
cases.description: Backspace right after a correction removes the space and puts the word back as typed; ending it again leaves it alone.

cases.name: undo-after-punctuation
cases.description: The undo works after punctuation too.

cases.name: no-undo-after-enter
cases.description: After Enter there is no undo: Backspace is just Backspace.

cases.name: undo-only-on-the-next-key
cases.description: Any key between the correction and Backspace ends the chance to undo.

cases.name: undo-restores-apostrophes
cases.description: The undo puts back exactly what was typed, apostrophes included.

cases.name: backspace-inside-a-word
cases.description: Backspace inside a word removes its last character.

cases.name: backspace-into-an-earlier-word
cases.description: Backspace with no word left deletes into text the keyboard does not know: nothing is corrected until the next word end.

cases.name: cursor-key-starts-fresh
cases.description: A cursor key forgets the word; the next character starts a new one.

cases.name: shortcut-starts-fresh
cases.description: A shortcut forgets the word, and the next word is corrected normally.

cases.name: click-starts-fresh
cases.description: A mouse click forgets the word.

cases.name: macro-text-is-not-typing
cases.description: A macro's text never counts as typing, and the word around it is forgotten.

cases.name: held-key-suspends
cases.description: A key held until the computer repeats it types characters the keyboard does not see, so the word is left alone.
cases.keyboardOnly: a key held until the computer repeats it

cases.name: keys-during-a-correction
cases.description: Keys pressed while a correction is typed come out afterwards, in order, and are corrected in their turn.

cases.name: held-shift-stays-out
cases.description: A Shift held across the correction does not change it, and is still held afterwards.

cases.name: held-shift-stays-out-of-a-macro-replacement
cases.description: A Shift held across a macro replacement does not change what the macro types, and is still held afterwards.

cases.name: macro-key-during-a-correction
cases.description: A macro key pressed while a correction is typed waits its turn behind the ending key.
cases.keyboardOnly: a macro key pressed during a correction

cases.name: full-queue
cases.description: More key changes than the queue holds arrive while the longest replacement is typed: the replacement stops where it is and no key is lost or reordered.

list.correction: Kind regards, Sam Example | +31 6 1234 5678 | sam@example.com | Example Street 12, 1234 AB Amsterdam, The Netherlands | KvK 0000

cases.name: no-undo-after-a-click-meanwhile-with-letters-kept
cases.description: The same when the replacement kept the word's first letter: Backspace removes the space and nothing else.

cases.name: typing-over-the-longest-replacement
cases.description: Keys typed while the longest replacement is typed, which takes over a second, all come out after it in order. The replacement is digits and hyphens, so no key typed meanwhile is one it is holding.

cases.name: macro-replacement
cases.description: A typed form whose replacement is a macro: the typed form is erased, the macro plays, then the ending key.
cases.result: Kind regards, Sam, Kind regards, Sam

cases.name: macro-replacement-has-no-case
cases.description: A macro plays as it is stored, whatever the case of the typed form.
cases.result: Kind regards, Sam Kind regards, Sam

cases.name: macro-replacement-has-no-undo
cases.description: After a macro replacement Backspace is only Backspace.

cases.name: macro-replacement-ended-by-enter
cases.description: Enter after a macro replacement comes after the macro.

cases.name: macro-replacement-ended-by-a-shifted-key
cases.description: The Shift of the key that ended the word stays out of the macro, and is back for that key.

cases.name: macro-replacement-ended-by-shift-enter
cases.description: Shift+Enter after a macro replacement: the macro plays without the Shift, then Enter.

cases.name: keys-during-a-macro-replacement
cases.description: Keys pressed while the typed form is erased and its macro plays come out afterwards, in order, and are corrected in their turn.
cases.result: Kind regards, Sam and the rest

cases.name: macro-replacement-empty-slot
cases.description: A replacement whose macro slot is empty is passed over: the typed form stays.

cases.name: macro-replacement-apostrophes
cases.description: An apostrophe before the typed form stays; with one after it the macro does not play, since erasing would take it along.

cases.name: macro-replacement-whole-word-only
cases.description: A macro plays for the whole word only, never inside a longer one.

cases.name: leader-sends-at-once
cases.description: After the Leader key nothing typed reaches the computer; a typed form after the leader that no longer one begins with is sent on its last character.

cases.name: leader-longest-sends-at-once
cases.description: abcd is the longest that begins with abcd, so it is sent on its last character.

cases.name: leader-enter-sends-the-shorter
cases.description: abc begins abcd, so it waits; Enter sends abc and never reaches the computer.

cases.name: leader-enter-on-no-typed-form
cases.description: Enter with what is held no typed form ends leading with nothing sent, Enter included.

cases.name: leader-timeout-sends-the-shorter
cases.description: The leader's timeout, counted from the last key, sends a typed form a longer one begins with.

cases.name: leader-timeout-on-no-typed-form
cases.description: The timeout with what is held no typed form ends leading with nothing sent.

cases.name: leader-early-exit
cases.description: A character that leaves what is held the start of no typed form ends leading at once, that character dropped too.

cases.name: leader-escape
cases.description: Escape ends leading with nothing sent and never reaches the computer.

cases.name: leader-backspace
cases.description: Backspace takes back the last character held, and with none held ends leading; neither reaches the computer.

cases.name: leader-again-starts-over
cases.description: Leader again drops what is held and starts over.

cases.name: leader-tab-is-itself
cases.description: Tab ends leading with nothing sent and reaches the computer as itself.

cases.name: leader-cursor-key-is-itself
cases.description: A key that types no character ends leading with nothing sent and acts as itself: Left moves the cursor.

cases.name: leader-click
cases.description: A mouse click ends leading with nothing sent.

cases.name: leader-macro-key
cases.description: A macro key ends leading with nothing sent and plays.

cases.name: leader-stored-switch-off
cases.description: With text replacement off in the profile the leader still sends; the word before it is left as typed.

cases.name: leader-override-off
cases.description: With text replacement switched off by key the leader still sends.

cases.name: leader-macro
cases.description: A typed form after the leader may name a macro, which plays with nothing to erase.

cases.name: leader-keys-during-a-send
cases.description: Keys typed while what the leader matched is typed come out after it, in order.

cases.name: leader-whatever-the-case
cases.description: What is held matches whatever its case: Shift and Caps Lock do not matter, and the replacement is typed as written.

cases.name: leader-under-caps-lock
cases.description: Under Caps Lock the replacement still shows as written.

cases.name: leader-no-undo
cases.description: There is no undo: Backspace after what the leader sent is Backspace.

cases.name: leader-without-leader-inputs
cases.description: With no typed form after the leader in the list the Leader key does nothing.

cases.name: leader-dead-key
cases.description: A dead key and the key it composes with are held as the one character they make.

cases.name: leader-dutch-space-drops
cases.description: Every leader input is a word, on any layout: a space leaves what is held the start of none and drops it, the space too.

cases.name: leader-only-never-as-you-type
cases.description: A replacement that fires only after the Leader key leaves its input as typed when a word ends, while one that fires as a word ends still does; after the Leader key it sends.

cases.name: leader-both-ways
cases.description: A replacement that fires both ways replaces its input as a word ends and sends it after the Leader key.

cases.name: leader-both-ways-part-of-word
cases.description: An input that matches part of a word, of a replacement that fires both ways: in a word as you type, and whole after the Leader key.
